title: helm(private): stabilize values schema + templating for init hooks and upgrade/rollback
author: Asha Patel
commits: a1b2c3: add JSON schema validation for private.values (values.schema.json) | d4e5f6: refactor initJobs templating to support conditional hooks and KMS config | f7g8h9: add upgrade/rollback stubs and pre-upgrade checks docs | i0j1k2: add unit tests for templates and schema; fix linting issues | l3m4n5: tweak README and rollback notes based on QA feedback
description: Motivation: Private deployments rely on a stable Helm values schema and deterministic init hook behavior for encryption init, Postgres backups, and upgrade/rollback safety. This PR stabilizes the values.schema.json, simplifies templating around conditional initJobs and hooks, and adds clear upgrade/rollback guidance. Summary of changes: 1) Values schema: add explicit top-level keys for kms.enabled, kms.provider, postgres.backup.enabled, initHooks.backoffLimit and upgrade.precheck.enabled; normalize types and add examples to improve validation and UX. 2) Templating: refactor templates/_helpers.tpl to centralize conditional helpers, switch init-jobs.yaml to use named hooks with deletion policies that are compatible with Helm upgrade/rollback flows, and add a postgresql backup hook that is guarded by .Values.postgres.backup.enabled. 3) Upgrade/rollback: add tests and docs describing recommended sequence for zero-downtime upgrades and safe rollbacks; include helm best-practices such as orphaned job cleanup and CRD-awareness. 4) Tests and CI: unit tests for template rendering against the schema and a small integration test harness for the hooks. 5) Backwards compatibility: keep legacy keys supported by mapping deprecated entries to new schema with warnings in README. Checklist: - [x] Add values.schema.json and examples - [x] Implement templating helpers and update initJobs/hooks - [x] Add unit tests and basic integration test for upgrade/rollback - [x] Update README and upgrade notes - [x] Run CI and fix lint failures How this affects upgrades: The schema tightening will cause new values that do not match to fail Helm lint/validate; existing installs will continue to work because deprecated fields are translated by the helpers, but operators should run the included pre-upgrade check (helm template --validate) and follow the precheck doc. Rollback behavior: init hook jobs now use hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation and hook-succeeded to avoid leftover jobs causing repeated execution after rollback. Security: KMS configuration is unchanged but the schema validates presence of kms.provider when kms.enabled is true. Testing notes: initial CI run surfaced two template lint failures and a flaky test that depended on implicit defaulting; those were fixed in commits i0j1k2 and l3m4n5. Related work: builds on ENG-2143 (helm schema stabilization) and ENG-2197 (init hook rollback improvements).
review_comments: Michael Chen: Left a couple of nits around helper naming and one question about hook-delete-policy semantics; suggest adding explicit tests for the before-hook-creation flow.
Sofia Ramirez: Verified values.schema.json against our internal validator; one optional field (postgres.backup.cron) should be nullable - updated in commit i0j1k2.
Evan Gupta: Approved after test fixes; asked to include a short runbook snippet for operators to follow during upgrades - added to README.
Asha Patel (author): Addressed all comments; expanded test coverage and documented rollback steps in charts/redwood-private/tests/upgrade-rollback.md.
release_notes: - Stabilize Helm values schema for redwood-private (kms, postgres backup, initHooks) | - Refactor init hook templating to improve upgrade/rollback safety and reduce orphaned jobs | - Add pre-upgrade checks and operator docs for safer upgrades
